items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: to put us together for a Sunday night there, which is where I met him. We’ve just continued the relationship for a long time.

ctx.x: Tell us about your association with Scott Hamilton and how that came about.

Well, I was working at Condon’s at the time and the fellow that worked the door and sort of managed the place, used to run the Half Note, Mike Cantarino was his name. And Mike was running — the Condon band worked Tuesday through Saturday, and on Sundays Mike would book another band. And Mike had heard Scott play with Hank Jones over at Michael’s Pub and thought it would be a good idea since we were more or less the same age, to put us together for a Sunday night there, which is where I met him. We’ve just…

It’s a good match. You guys are playing a kind of music we mentioned earlier, that we don’t know what to call it. But it comes from a time that was before your formative years I guess. What’s the most modern type situation you’ve ever found yourself in? Is that a fair term? Or contemporary —

items.title: Scott Hamilton interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: in this case Kenny Davern, the clarinetist, and Warren Vache was playing cornet — I was hoping that they would have routines because I’m sort of filling in for where in this group it’s usually a trombone player

ctx.x: play something in unison, and then you just split into three part harmony. How did you know how to find your part? I mean there was nothing written, was it rehearsed or did you just know — I’m going to take the fifth, you take the seventh—

I don’t know for sure. I was actually hoping that — in this case Kenny Davern, the clarinetist, and Warren Vache was playing cornet — I was hoping that they would have routines because I’m sort of filling in for where in this group it’s usually a trombone player, and I’m not quite sure all the time when they’re going to go into one of those things and when they’re not. But when they do, and when they jump on it, I can usually get the third note pretty fast. I wait, basically, for Kenny to start playing harmony to…
